blocks.title: Seated Achilles toe press against wall
blocks.display_name: Seated Achilles toe press against wall
coaching_cues: Sit on the floor with your legs comfortably extended and your feet against a wall, supporting yourself with your arms. Gently press your toes into the wall without moving your ankle. Hold for 10 seconds, relax, and repeat 10 times, once daily. Use comfortable low effort; no pushing through pain, step, deep heel drop, added weight or forceful stretching. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the work. Follow clinician restrictions.

blocks.title: Gentle forearm rotation with supported dowel
blocks.display_name: Gentle forearm rotation with supported dowel
coaching_cues: Sit with your elbow bent at a right angle beside your body. Hold a lightweight dowel at its centre with a relaxed grip and support its weight with your other hand. Slowly turn the affected palm upwards and downwards through a small comfortable range. Work pain-free at your own pace; no set count or hold is required. Do not use the dowel as a lever, add a band or weights, force the range, grip hard or twist quickly. Stop for increasing pain, swelling, tingling or loss of function; follow clinician restrictions.

blocks.title: Supported comfortable shoulder wall slide
coaching_cues: Stand facing a smooth wall with a cloth under the affected hand. Gently slide the hand upwards only through a comfortable range no higher than shoulder level, then return. Do not lean body weight heavily into the arm, force a painful arc, add resistance or lift overhead. Keep the neck comfortable; no forced chin tuck or posture correction is required. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the movement. Seek assessment for catching, locking, loss of function, altered sensation, a hot swollen joint or fever.

blocks.title: Gentle supine adductor ball squeeze
coaching_cues: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet in line with your knees. Place a soft ball between your knees. Gently squeeze it, hold for up to 5 seconds, then fully relax. Keep the exercise pain-free and self-paced, little and often; stop before fatigue rather than forcing a repetition target. Do not bridge, pulse, use an unstable surface or squeeze maximally. Stop if groin pain increases during or after the exercise. Follow clinician restrictions.

drill.notes: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet in line with your knees. Place a soft ball between your knees. Gently squeeze it, hold for up to 5 seconds, then fully relax. Keep the exercise pain-free and self-paced, little and often; stop before fatigue rather than forcing a repetition target. Do not bridge, pulse, use an unstable surface or squeeze maximally. Stop if groin pain increases during or after the exercise. Follow clinician restrictions.
regress_when: Stop and return to conservative guidance if symptoms worsen.
stop_when: Stop if pain or symptoms increase during or after the exercise. Follow your existing clinician restrictions.
drill.evidence_notes: Sources: https://www.berkshirehealthcare.nhs.uk/advice/groin-strain, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10569248/. Fixed conservative movement only. No change to stage-entry criteria or permission, and no inference of sport readiness. Numeric guidance is source-backed where present; otherwise explicitly self-paced. No automatic resistance, range or speed progression.
